_readme: Single source of truth for the Projects section. Edit this file and commit — there is no build step.
Order here is the order on the page; the 01-05 numbers on the cards are generated from it.
title / type show in the case-study modal. Add shortTitle / shortType only when the card should say something briefer.
thumbnail is one of:  { video, poster }  |  { image }  |  { color, glyph }   (color: yellow | ink | blue)
size sets the card width: lg | md | sm
about / features / links / gallery fill the case-study modal. gallery is optional.
tags are the domain labels that drift in on clouds beside the panel — keep to 1-2, they share the hero's vocabulary (UI/UX, AI, ML, SWE).
notes are the hand-drawn callouts on each screenshot: text (\n for a line break), x/y are % positions of the label, from = which side the arrow reaches in.
logo is optional: an app icon shown beside the title on the card and in the case study.
gallery { type: images, frame: phone } shows screens in a phone; give an item a dark src to get a Light/Dark switch.

projects.title: AppNest
projects.tagline: Job tracker that parses emails on-device. Designed in Figma, built in SwiftUI.
projects.about: An iOS job application tracker I designed and built end to end. Paste a confirmation email and Apple's on-device NaturalLanguage framework pulls out the company, role, status and pay, with no API calls and no account. Paste a Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby or Workday link and it fills itself in. Everything is stored locally with SwiftData. The UI runs on a token-based design system that I mirrored in Figma (light and dark modes as one variable switch, components mapped to their Swift views).
features: On-device email parsing with NLTagger, regex and NSDataDetector: nothing leaves the phone
ATS link parsing for Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and Workday
CSV import with a forgiving column mapper and an editable preview, plus CSV export
Search cycles ("Summer 2026") with bulk edit, move and delete
Per-application interview prep notes and follow-up reminders
Figma design system: semantic color tokens with light/dark modes, components mapped 1:1 to SwiftUI views
Dynamic Type throughout and 44pt minimum touch targets

projects.title: OIS Competition
projects.tagline: Turns a store sales metric into a live team competition.
projects.about: A game-like web app I built for my retail job at Hollister. Associates log their daily OIS (orders in store), the app computes sales per hour, and the whole team watches a live leaderboard. It now runs multiple stores, each with its own roster, competitions and manager PIN. Teammates' names are blurred in these screenshots.
features: Multi-store: each store has its own data, roster and manager PIN
Automatic sales-per-hour from logged orders and hours
Real-time leaderboard on Firebase, updated for everyone at once
Countdown, store-wide goal meter and an end-of-competition podium
PIN-gated manager tools for players, logs and competitions
Mobile-first arcade UI built for a quick tap between customers

projects.title: Groov
projects.tagline: Letterboxd for albums: discover, rate and shelve what you hear.
projects.about: An iOS app for logging the albums you listen to, built as my capstone for CodePath's iOS 101. Discover pulls trending albums from the Last.fm API, search covers albums and artists, and every album gets a detail page with a five-star rating and a To Listen button. Your library persists on-device.
features: Trending albums from the Last.fm API in a Discover grid
Debounced live search, filterable by album, artist or both
Album detail with art, description and a 1-5 star rating
Library split into Rated and To Listen, with swipe to delete
Persistence with Codable and UserDefaults
UIKit with Storyboards and a custom vinyl app icon

projects.title: NoteWeb
projects.tagline: Local-first semantic search. Nothing leaves your machine.
projects.about: A local-first RAG tool that semantically indexes and searches your documents using LLaMA 3 and vector embeddings. Everything runs locally: no cloud, and no data leaves your machine.
features: Semantic search across local documents
LLaMA 3 for local LLM inference
Vector embeddings for document indexing
Fully offline, no cloud dependencies
RAG pipeline from ingestion to query

projects.title: Spotify Hit Song Predictor
projects.tagline: Can audio features predict a hit? Mostly no, and that was the finding.
projects.about: A logistic regression study of whether Spotify audio features (danceability, energy, valence, tempo and more) can predict a hit. They can't, at least not alone: no single feature correlates with hit status above 0.10, and even with engineered interaction terms the model lands at ROC AUC 0.53, barely above chance. Class imbalance pushed it to predict "not a hit" almost every time, which made accuracy a misleading metric.
features: Full pipeline in a Jupyter notebook: cleaning, EDA, feature engineering, model, evaluation
Correlation analysis showing no audio feature strongly tracks hit status
Interaction features (energy x danceability, valence x energy) and their learned weights
Evaluated with ROC/AUC, precision-recall and a confusion matrix, not accuracy alone
Takeaway: popularity depends on things audio features don't capture, like marketing, timing and the artist
